entries.topicDescription: Architecture component for managing UI-related data across configuration changes.

tips.title: StateFlow vs LiveData
tips.content:
Both StateFlow and LiveData hold observable state, but StateFlow
is Kotlin-first and works well with coroutines.

StateFlow always has a value (no null initial state).
It's lifecycle-unaware — use collectAsStateWithLifecycle() in Compose
or repeatOnLifecycle() in Views to collect safely.

LiveData is lifecycle-aware out of the box but is Java-based
and doesn't integrate as naturally with coroutines and Flow.

tips.title: SavedStateHandle for process death
tips.content:
ViewModel survives rotation but NOT process death.
Android can kill your app's process in the background.

SavedStateHandle persists data across process death.
It acts like a map — get/set values that are saved to
the saved-state bundle automatically.

Use it for: search queries, selected tab index,
scroll position — anything the user would expect to survive.

tips.title: ViewModel basics — survive rotation
tips.content:
ViewModel stores and manages UI-related data. It survives
configuration changes like screen rotation.

A ViewModel is scoped to an Activity or Fragment. It's created
the first time the scope requests it and lives until the scope
is permanently destroyed (e.g., Activity finishes).

Put UI state and business logic calls in the ViewModel.
Keep the Activity/Fragment thin — just observing and rendering state.
